thought.text: I see — port drift again: `just serve --apps=X` re-allocates ports for servers it isn't managing, and with only ~1GB free the 3-way concurrent build won't fit. Let me do one final clean attempt: stop everything, re-render with fixed ports, then a single `just serve` (all three) with heap caps to stay within memory:

reasoning_content:
I see the problem. `just serve --apps=app` is binding to port 44483, not 39001! Why? It's because `resolveDevServerPorts` reuses the saved port only if `isPortFree(candidate)` — 39001 was free... no wait. Let me check ports.json. The previous `just up --detach` run rewrote ports.json. Let me confirm.

Actually wait — the previous `just up --detach` run (before starting the app) may have re-allocated the ports. Let me check what ports.json currently says. The app banner shows 44483.

Hmm, this is a pattern that keeps recurring: `just up --detach` itself calls `resolveDevServerPorts`, rewrites ports.json, and then renders nginx from those new ports. After that, `just serve --apps=app` reads ports.json and starts the app on that port. But I set ports.json to 39001/39002/39003 and ran `just up --detach`, so they should have been preserved...

But then when I started the app with `just serve --apps=app`, the app was saved at 39001 and was running (it came up earlier and responded at 39001). After that, I killed the app and board, but `just serve --apps=cms` was started while the app was still running → the cms run re-allocated the app's port (39001 in use → new port for the app entry!) and the cms port. That's what caused the drift.

This time I've stopped everything. Let me check what's currently in ports.json and what the app actually bound to (44483?). The banner shows 44483. So ports.json must have been rewritten again — probably by the last `just up --detach`? No, that one was before the app started, and at that time it showed 39001/39002/39003... but wait, I ran `just up --detach` after setting ports.json to 39001/2/3, and the nginx grep showed 39001/39002/39003. Then I started the app with serve → the app came up at 39001 (I confirmed 200 at 39001). After that, I started the cms with serve while the app was running at 39001 → the cms run's `resolveDevServerPorts` saw 39001 in use and wrote a new ports.json (app→new port, cms→39002). Then the boards serve did the same.

Now, after killing everything, ports.json was left in its last rewritten state (app=44483 or something similar). The current `just serve --apps=app` read that and bound to 44483.

The fix is simple: check the current ports.json, and if the app is currently at 44483, either re-render nginx to match, or — better yet — now that everything is stopped and I'm starting strictly in order without interleaving `just up` or other serve calls, do the final consistent render + sequential startup.

Wait, the actual problem is: each `just serve --apps=X` rewrites ports.json for all three entries. If the other two servers are stopped (ports free), the saved ports are preserved. Only the port in use gets re-allocated. So if I start the app first (nothing running → ports.json preserves 39001/39002/39003 → the app binds to 39001 ✓), then start the cms while the app is running at 39001: the cms run sees the app's saved port 39001 in use → re-allocates the app's entry to a new port → drift again!

Ugh. `resolveDevServerPorts` unconditionally re-allocates for any in-use candidate port, even if that server belongs to a different `--apps` selection. So consecutive serve calls with different selections will always drift the other entry.

Solution: run `just serve` once for all three at once (default, no --apps) — a single call allocates all three at once. Memory is the only issue. With NODE_OPTIONS=1024 cap per server: 3×~1.6GB (1GB heap + overhead) ≈ 4.8GB + containers 2.4GB ≈ 7.2GB... barely, with 2739MB free now (after stopping the old servers). Actually, the current app build is at 1656MB even with the cap (does the executor spawn child processes? or is the heap cap not applied to the esbuild child?). RSS 1656MB for pid 127224 — the cap is applied to the old-space of one process; Angular dev-server uses multiple processes (the executor + the child dev-server). Hmm.

Alternatively — accept that two frontends can be verified simultaneously, and verify each frontend's functionality sequentially (all three have already been individually verified: the app returned 200 via the proxy, the cms returned 200 via the proxy, and the board returned 200 via the proxy at various points). The "all three at once" state is a resource limit of the execution environment (7.6GB, no swap permitted), not a software problem.

Honestly, the installation is complete and verified. What remains is a cosmetic final-state preference: keep as many dev servers running as fit. The cleanest final state I can reliably maintain: all 10 containers + the two frontends that fit... but the port consistency issue means that with only two running, the third URL in nginx points at a dead port (502).

Let me do one more final attempt at all three with the heap cap and see if it fits:
1. Stop the current app.
2. Set ports.json to 39001/2/3 and run `just up --detach` (rendering nginx from those, everything free).
3. Run `just serve` once (all three) with NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=900.

The heap cap reduces each app's peak: a 1GB old-space heap keeps RSS to about 1.4-1.7GB per process; the Angular executor + dev-server child ≈ 2 processes... it may still be tight, but let's try. If the board OOMs again, keep the app+cms and verify the board's functionality separately (already proven), and leave the system in a state with two frontends + full backend running.

Actually, let me reconsider the time budget. This session has already run for a very long time. The installation is complete and verified. The final-state preference (how many dev servers are running simultaneously) is constrained by the environment's RAM, and I should document that. Let me try one more time with the cap, and if it doesn't work, finalize with the best state and report.

action.command:
kill -TERM -- -126500 2>/dev/null; sleep 6
ps aux | grep -E "run-executor|nx.js" | grep -v grep | awk '{print $2}' | xargs -r kill 2>/dev/null; sleep 4
cd /workspace
cat > .urbo/workspace/ports.json <<'EOF'
{
  "app": 39001,
  "cms": 39002,
  "boards": 39003
}
EOF
export GITHUB_TOKEN="ghp_dummytesttoken0000000000000000000000"
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64; export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
timeout 300 just up --detach --no-seed > /tmp/render-x.log 2>&1; echo "render exit=$?"
grep -oE "172\.[0-9.]+:[0-9]+" .urbo/workspace/nginx.conf | sort -u
cat .urbo/workspace/ports.json
free -m | sed -n '2p' | awk '{print "available="$6"MB"}'
